subject: Clarify pass/fail checklist and test catalog for Clarity Health evaluation
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Clarify pass/fail checklist and test catalog for Clarity Health evaluation

Sara — thanks again for the time this morning. Per our discussion, I’m sending a compact test catalog and a pass/fail checklist so we can lock the go/no-go gates for the 4-week evaluation. Attached: MAP_Clarity_v0.3.xlsx (mutual action plan), and a CSV of the initial test cases.

Goal for this thread: agree on measurable success criteria, identify owners for each test, and confirm timing so procurement can align on licensing/terms. Please review and reply with any additional success metrics you need included.

High-level proposal (from Redwood):
- Core SLA: median 95th percentile token latency <= 450ms for the clinical routing flow
- Quality: F1 >= 0.88 on our shared de-identified sample for entity extraction tasks (N=500 examples)
- Robustness: <2% failure rate on long-form prompts (>1k tokens)
- Safety/regulatory: PII redaction accuracy >= 99% for matching PHI fields

Suggested owners:
- Redwood runbook & perf tests: Ben Carter
- Clinical eval/case set: Clarity (Sara) + Marissa for test design support
- Security evidence (log & retention): Monica Patel

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP and test owners
- Week 1: seed data exchange and baseline perf run
- Week 2: iterative tuning + regression checks
- Week 3: final verification and signoff prep
- Week 4: decision meeting (go/no-go)

Please indicate any non-negotiable thresholds or alternate metrics you need. If procurement needs a single consolidated artifact, we can produce a condensed SLA appendix for the contract.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP_Clarity_v0.3.xlsx (spreadsheet), test-catalog-clarity.csv (csv)

Subject: Re: Clarify pass/fail checklist and test catalog for Clarity Health evaluation

Hannah — this looks great and very actionable. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) On quality: can you confirm how you compute F1 for the entity extraction? We run a stricter span-level match for clinical entities and need to ensure parity.
2) On latency: the 95th percentile metric is fine, but we need a 99th percentile for peak-hour traffic (we’ll provide a 2-hour sample trace). Can Redwood measure both?
3) For robustness: we’ll include synthetic long-case scenarios — can you include a separate long-tail failure log we can inspect?

Procurement wanted me to flag that any SLA referenced in the MAP should be mirrored in the draft contract appendix so they can route redlines. I’ve CC’d procurement for visibility — they’ll need the condensed SLA artifact you mentioned.

Also — two small asks: could you add a short list of runbook steps that qualify as an automatic fallback (e.g., model variant downgrade) and a proposal for how rollbacks are triggered? We want the decision tree upfront.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Barnes | Director, Clinical Automation, Clarity Health

Thanks — quick details from the Redwood test & ops side. I pulled sample baselines from our internal perf harness against a comparable clinical model: median 95th ~380ms, 99th ~1200ms under synth peak. We can run both metrics against your 2-hour peak trace.

Proposed concrete pass criteria (to put in the MAP appendix):
- Perf: 95th percentile <= 450ms AND 99th percentile <= 1.5s on your peak-hour trace (measured server-side, p95/p99 across requests)
- Quality: entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 using span-aware scoring (we’ll share the scoring script)
- Regression tolerance: any release showing >3% drop vs baseline on key metrics triggers a human review and rollback window (48 hours)
- Data sync: Clarity provides a 500-record de-identified gold set by EOW; Redwood returns annotated outputs and a diff report within 72 hours of receipt

Runbook excerpt (fallbacks):
1) Automatic model downgrade to smaller variant if p99 > 2s for >5 minutes
2) Switch routing to dedicated reserved pool if error rate spikes above 1%
3) If quality regression detected post-tuning, revert to pinned model version and schedule root-cause review

Owners: Ben (perf runs & p99 measurement), Marissa (scoring scripts & test harness), Monica (security & logs).

I attached a starter test-catalog export (test-catalog-clarity.csv) with example cases and the scoring script link in the MAP. Happy to hop on a short session to walk through the scoring approach if that helps.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: test-catalog-clarity.csv (csv)

Procurement also requested a single point of contact for security evidence during the trial. Monica — would you be the contact?

We also propose adding a small acceptance test for hallucination checks: spot-check 100 generated summaries for clinically incorrect assertions; acceptable failure rate <= 2.5%.

If all of that looks good, procurement will prioritize the contract appendix so we can avoid delays.
